passages.heading: FLORIDA WANTS AN HONEST CHOICE FOR GOVERNOR ...NOT A PARTY OWNED YES-MAN.
passages.text: Not accepting contributions Not affiliated or controlled by the Democrat or Republican Party

passages.heading: Charles Burkett is like:
passages.text: Fishback without the Baggage. Collins's Patriotism. Renner's Gravitas. Donalds without his baggage and being bought and paid for. Jolly without the sellout to the woke, hard Left fanatics.

passages.heading: What I am is a concerned homeowner, hardworking parent, lifetime Florida resident, unhappy overcrowded, over-trafficked commuter, successful problem-solver, successful investor, and experienced 'sleazy politician detector,' who unlike most, refuses to go along - just to get along.
passages.text: In other words, I am not influenced by the "political crowd" in the least. As a matter of fact, with few exceptions, I have the same deep distaste as everyone else for most of that group, who are usually simply pretenders and posers, set on trying to show the world, at every possible moment, how absolutely wonderful they are.

passages.heading: I'm not going to Tallahassee because I need friends, or to impress or be impressed, or to make a living.
passages.text: I'm running for office because voters want an experienced problem-solver and need someone they can trust - I mean really trust. Someone who will tell them the truth. Someone who will work for them and be "their" insider, not a political weasel telling voters what they want to hear and then, doing the exact opposite.

passages.heading: My entire 43-year volunteer and political history is built on trust, honesty, and a reputation for telling it like it is, good, bad or ugly.
passages.text: I am not perfect. But, as one standing for elected office, I will put my four decades of public service up against anyone vying to demonstrate fidelity to voters who long for a leader that they can trust.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I was born at St. Francis Hospital (which is now Aqua, on 63rd Street, near Collins Avenue) and raised in Miami Beach.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I moved to Surfside in 1996 to take advantage of the unparalleled lifestyle and have lived here, in the same home, ever since.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: Julia and I are the proud parents of William Michael Burkett (now 22). I enjoy skiin

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: Julia and I are the proud parents of William Michael Burkett (now 22). I enjoy skiing, diving, flying, boating & great food.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: Pre-school: The Cushman School, Miami Grammar: St. Patrick's School, Miami Beach High: Archbishop Curley High School, Miami College: University of Miami, BS, Finance

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: After I graduated from college, I used my savings from working as a construction site laborer to buy my first property in 1983. It was a home in Miami Beach that I renovated, with help from friends I hired, and then leased.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I then purchased my first building in Miami Beach's budding Art Deco District with the remainder of my sa

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I then purchased my first building in Miami Beach's budding Art Deco District with the remainder of my savings. I renovated that building, was able to get a loan on the equity I created in the property, and bought my next property.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I did this over and over throughout the 80s, 90s and early 2000s.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I subsequently went on to expand on a national basis into an additional seven states.

passages.heading: My Personal Story
passages.text: I currently operate a national investment company, which I own 100% of, which oversees those investments.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: A board member and chairman of the Miami Beach Housing Authority for nine years, A board member of the Nuisance Abatement Board, Member of the Code Enforcement Board, Member of the Community Development Block Grant Board, A Miami Beach Police Academy member, A board member of the Miami Beach Chamber, The President of the North Beach Development Corporation, A board member of my neighborhood association, the La Gorce-Pinetree Homeowners Association, I have also participated in many blue ribbon & ad hoc committees in Miami Beach over my 35 years living there.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: When I moved to Surfside in 1996, my civic involvement was as follows:

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: In 2004, I ran for Mayor of Surfside and lost my first election by a hair. In 2006, I was first elected Mayor of Surfside. In 2008, I was re-elected Mayor of Surfside. In 2020, I was re-elected Mayor of Surfside and guided our residents through the Covid disaster and the collapse of an entire condominum building, the third worst in U.S. history, which resulted in the loss of 98 lives. In 2024, I was re-elected Mayor of Surfside. I'm proud of my record of service in Surfside to protect our town and its residents from exploitative predators interested only in financial gain at the cost of our precious small-town way of life.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: Surfside is a Florida gem and I intend to bring the same skills that made it that way to our entire state.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: While I serve as Surfside's mayor, my one and only interest is the success and well-being of our Town.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: However, like all red-blooded, patriotic Americans, I love our Country, and want the best for it and our citizens.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: Now that my service to Surfside is complete, I am running for Florida Governor. I know that I can bring the passion and love I have dedicated to our beautiful Surfside hamlet on the beach, and its successes, to all the citizens of Florida.

passages.heading: My Political Story
passages.text: You can read more about the views and positions I would put forward in the Governor's campaign at my political positions website:

passages.heading: Keep Florida affordable.
passages.text: Slash and eventually eliminate property taxes for vested Florida homeowners and renters. For each year beyond a year-ten residency vesting period requirement, Florida homeowners would be entitled to a cumulative 10%-point increase of their existing homestead exemption, until their adjusted exemption reaches 100%. Renters in Florida, who meet a ten-year residency vesting period requirement and who go on to purchase a Florida home, would also enjoy the same cumulative 10%-point increase of their new home's homestead exemption, until their adjusted exemption reaches 100%. Additionally, the adjusted homestead exemption shall be transferable to the homeowner's wife or children.

passages.heading: Rewrite the broken laws and bring radical competition into the property and auto insurance market.
passages.text: Make Florida's current residents, and not new arrivals, a priority in all decisions. Stop the current radical new construction boom which is turning our roads into parking lots. Choose renovation over new construction to first fix what we have, contain overgrowth and preserve the quality of life that is slowly slipping away from each Floridian due to the "Manhattanization" of our beautiful villages, towns, cities, and eventually given enough time, our entire State.

passages.heading: Reverse damage that monied interests and influential lobbyists have inflicted on local communities.
passages.text: Listen and act upon the best ideas from all voices ...and Parties. Encourage camaraderie and collegiality from all elected officials in an effort to foster agreement wherever possible. Reject virulent tribalism, damaging Party politics, and views that are antithetical to our Country's founding values. Sensibly balance the power structure between Tallahassee and local governments.

passages.heading: Hold government accountable, delivering high quality services while controlling costs to residents.
passages.text: Promote tourism, business and economic development, and sensible, responsible growth, but never at the expense or to the detriment of our Florida residents.

passages.heading: Tell the truth as to why condo owners are under financial attack after the Surfside collapse.
passages.text: Copy Texas and create the Florida Bullion Depository. This will allow all Florida residents, including Florida public employees, who wish to invest their savings in gold, silver or platinum a government sanctioned, safe and easily accessible way of storing and protecting their retirement savings.

passages.heading: A Florida education must focus only on kids, be a model of high standards, and keep costs in line.
passages.text: Give our first responders every tool they need to be the best in the business. Pay them, and all our public workers a fair, competitive wage. Honor (unsustainable) defined benefit pension promises to existing employees. Offer all new employees a menu of generous defined contribution plans which provide each employee with the ability to be vested immediately, to receive a generous match from government for each dollar they contribute, to take the plan with them if they leave their current job, and to have access to all of their funds decades before they otherwise would with existing plans.

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Eliminate property taxes on homesteaded primary residences. Benefit passes down to children. Completely rewrite broken property and auto insurance laws. Dismiss non-criminal traffic tickets for drivers with clean 10-year records. Eliminate unfair paid highway express lanes. Eliminate unfair tolls on public roads. Eliminate Florida’s unfair gas tax. Eliminate permit fees to repair and improve your home. Force local government to provide water and sewer at cost. Slash bloated government, wherever it is, that we don’t need – or want. Rewrite the unaffordable, broken healthcare laws. Put doctors, not government and insurance companies, in charge. Make ‘Right to Try’ laws absolute.

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Affirm and codify “My Body, My Choice.” Free Florida medical research from bureaucratic and litigious strangulation.

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Stop dangerous over-development that is destroying our way of life:

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Repeal the Live Local Act sham, and all others like it, put in place mostly to line the pockets of developers – who then gladly line the pockets of politicians. Stop the “Manhattanization” and continued “over-densification” of Florida’s charming and historic communities. Crush traffic and population gridlock by favoring smart renovation over unchecked new construction, and by favoring current residents over those who wish to move to Florida.

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Restore trust and ‘FedEx/UPS-style’ efficiency in government:

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Eliminate excessive pay and pension schemes that reward career politicians and others which will eventually bankrupt our state. Any government position paying more than $250,000 must not exceed a two-year term and be reviewed and advertised for replacement, with interviews of all new applicants, every two years . Prohibit politicians and bureaucrats from wasteful travel. Require all “meetings,” “retreats,” non-physical “training,” and “education,” be conducted by Zoom only.

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Promote common-sense growth and restoration :

passages.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passages.text: Real education for our kids, not factory-style, educational warehousing. Retain only great teachers — good enough is not good enough for our kids. Demand clean water and air. Transform Florida's slums, ghettos, and war zone neighborhoods by enacting my proposed "Oasis Act”. Employ economic development and tourism programs that benefit Floridians most — not developers, special interests, new Florida arrivals, or tourists. Data centers only permitted after a referendum vote and approval by the citizens of the targeted county and city.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The likely best two solutions are: allow radical competition between ALL legitimate and financially strong insurance carriers. Encourage a wide menu of deductibles, so that if customers wish, they can participate in risk in return for lower premiums.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Lawmakers must tell homeowners the truth; that not all homes and home locations can be made safe against hurricanes, and that there is not a good free market solution available for same.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Poorly constructed homes, homes in flood zones, homes near large bodies of water, are all poor risks (bets) and are likely going to be badly damaged in a hurricane, something all insurance companies will want to avoid, or charge unacceptably high premiums for.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: In the end, owners with hurricane resistant homes and safer locations will enjoy (relatively) competitive rates.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The other homeowners and their lenders must face the reality that short of a subsidy from government, whether in the form of premium assistance or financial assistance after a hurricane, there are few good options.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: To understand the dilemma in a nutshell, a homeowner could simply ask him/herself this question: if I had the $1,000,000 my neighbor’s home is insured for as cash in my bank account, what premium would I be willing to charge in return for handing over that entire $1,000,000 bank account to my neighbor in the case my neighbor’s home was hit by a hurricane?

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The truth is, most would not want to take on the risk for any premium.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: So, since there is no good free market solution for a large number of homes, what can be done?

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 1) For homes that can be satisfactorily fortified against hurricanes, the total cost of approved upgrades could be offset against the property’s real estate taxes. Of course, in the short run this would impact local municipalities, but have the long-term benefit of strengthening homes, improving taxable values and retaining residents and entire neighborhoods that could be displaced following a hurricane.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 2) For homes that are not candidates for fortification initiatives, and cannot buy affordable insurance, homeowners could be incentivized, one time, to buy a new, hurricane-proof home by providing them with an additional homestead exemption amount on their new home equal to the sale price of their existing home.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 3) All home lenders must make a determination prior to the issuance of any home loan that the property’s structure is hurricane resistant and following issuance of the loan, shall not be permitted to withdraw the loan or penalize a homeowner in any way, during the term of the loan, related to the hurricane resistance of the structure.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Radically Transform Florida’s Auto Insurance

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Goal: Protect responsible drivers from being financially penalized by uninsured motorists and create stronger accountability for those who drive without insurance.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The Problem is that Florida’s current auto insurance system allows too many drivers to operate vehicles without continuous coverage. This places an unfair financial burden on law-abiding drivers through higher insurance rates, while also creating safety risks on the roadways.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The system makes it relatively easy for uninsured drivers to maintain valid vehicle registrations, weakening enforcement and accountability.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: My proposed reforms require annual, Non-Cancellable insurance policies.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Insurance companies would only be permitted to issue 12-month auto insurance policies. These policies would be non-cancellable by the insurance company and policyholder during the term, except in cases of total loss or sale of the vehicle.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Require Proof of Full-Year Insurance to Obtain or Renew Registration.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Drivers must provide proof of a full 12-month auto insurance policy before receiving a new or renewed Florida license tag sticker. Without this proof, the tax collector’s office would be prohibited from issuing the updated registration.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Tie Insurance Coverage Directly to the annual License Tag sticker renewal.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Insurance coverage would be directly linked to the vehicle’s registration. A vehicle’s registration would only remain valid when supported by continuous insurance coverage for the full registration period as evidenced by valid annual license tag sticker.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: An insurance company could only terminate its obligation to provide coverage before the end of the 12-month policy period if it physically obtains the vehicle’s license tag and current registration sticker from the policyholder. Until the insurance company takes possession of the tag and sticker, it would remain fully obligated to maintain coverage for the entire year.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Insurance companies would be responsible for collecting premiums and maintaining continuous coverage for the full 12-month period, matching the duration of the vehicle’s registration shown on the license tag sticker.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Any driver unable to provide proof of a full year of auto insurance would be ineligible to obtain or renew a license tag sticker. Without a current tag sticker, the vehicle could not legally be operated on Florida roadways.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The foregoing simple changes will significantly reduce the number of uninsured drivers by removing the ability to register a vehicle without maintaining full-year insurance coverage.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The changes create clear accountability by making it difficult for either the driver or the insurance company to create coverage gaps during the registration period.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The changes protect responsible drivers by reducing the cost-shifting caused by uninsured motorists.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The changes simplify enforcement for law enforcement, as vehicles without a current tag sticker would be clearly operating illegally.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: And in the end, strengthens the overall insurance market by rewarding compliance and holding non-compliant drivers accountable.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: “Healthcare” has become a meaningless term.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: It exists only in the fantasy world of policymakers whose laws make care far more costly and complicated than it should be.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Policymakers have forced insurers to cover pre-existing conditions—which is just like requiring car insurance to pay for crashes...that have already happened!

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: It sounds compassionate, but everyone knows that’s not how insurance actually works. Yet this is exactly the broken system we have today - thanks to politicians who take orders from their handlers.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Our elected leaders have so thoroughly wrecked the insurance market that it is now nearly incomprehensible. Trying to compare insurance policies is a fool’s errand.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The language is impenetrable, the costs obscene, and the situation keeps getting worse .

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Buying any policy is little more than an act of hope that it will actually pay the bills when you need it - and it probably won’t.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: What can be done? We absolutely, positively must return to basics.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 1) Restore real incentives for doctors—driven out of private practice by crushing costs, litigation, insurance companies, and red tape—to reopen small offices, treat patients directly, and bill as they see fit.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 2) Restore the sacred doctor-patient relationship, free from bureaucratic interference.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 3) Rewrite the unaffordable, broken healthcare laws. Put doctors, not government and insurance companies, in charge. Make ‘Right to Try’ laws absolute. Affirm and codify “My Body, My Choice.” Free Florida medical research from bureaucratic and litigious strangulation.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 4) Restore our insurance market back to pricing risk, reflected in policy premiums.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 5) For healthy individuals with no pre-existing conditions - rebuild a genuine insurance market.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Have Government create five clear, cookie-cutter standardized policy categories.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: For each category, create low-, medium-, and high-deductible versions—producing 15 easy-to-compare plans.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Insurers would then compete aggressively on price for each and offer them in the market:

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: a. Diamond Plan – Covers every healthcare circumstance.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: b. Platinum Plan – Covers most healthcare circumstances.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: c. Gold Plan – Covers most healthcare circumstances, excluding accidents.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: d. Silver Plan – Covers only accidents, not routine health issues.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: e. Bronze Plan – Covers 50% of the cost of most healthcare incidents or accidents.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: For people with pre-existing conditions, there is no traditional insurance option.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: True insurance is protection against unknown future events, not pre-existing conditions.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The truth is, the pre-existing conditions insurance term is nothing more than a government-mandated subsidy scheme, a forced wealth transfer from healthy people ( who pay grossly inflated premiums ) to people who are already sick.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Slippery politicians want you to believe that it is just another form of insurance - it is not .

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Worse, forcing this scheme into a legitimate market/risk-based insurance system destroys the risk-based market that functioned for centuries hurting more people than it helps.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: That said, a responsible safety net is essential . It must however be deliberately engineered to minimize moral hazard, and it will require real creativity.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Leverage the insurance companies' expertise in managing costs and their strong negotiated rates with providers.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Assign every person with a pre-existing condition to one of the insurers operating in the state.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: In return for a fair administrative fee, each company would manage, not pay for, care for an equal share of these patients.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: This 'care arrangement' would eliminate the crazy hospital pricing schemes, the extreme price shocks and anxiety patients face every day, like the well-known emergency room visit that gets billed to the patient for $21,000, and then is reduced for the insurance company to $1650! This one step alone could ignite a 'back to affordability' healthcare revolution!

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Every applicant would first be means-tested. Those who qualify could access a state-backed loan fund — up to $200,000 lifetime per person — administered jointly by the patient and their assigned insurer.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Repayment would be capped at 28% of net income until the loan is repaid.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: For those who do not qualify, or whose needs exceed that lifetime limit , they would necessarily enter a tightly managed state pool overseen by physicians and medical experts who would directly coordinate their care and make cost-conscious treatment decisions.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: This plan keeps private insurers handling day-to-day administration and negotiation, uses loans instead of grants to reduce moral hazard, only applies full government control for the most extreme cases, and leaves the insurance market healthy, competing, and functioning with the most competitive premiums, exactly like it should function.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Those newly competitive premiums, and easy to understand policies, could also induce the many who now go without coverage to go out and buy some!

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: In other words, this plan would bring back “ real ” insurance coverage and aggressive competition, which will see premiums reflect actual risk – not the unknown costs of subsidizing a market with no visible bottom.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: It also provides for fair, compassionate and cost effective healthcare coverage for the most sick and needy among us.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Affordable and workforce housing (AWH) are critical components of any successful community.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Not everyone can afford market housing options, hence the need for AWH options.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: To begin, AWH should be located near to the communities they serve. However, some believe that AWH should be built inside the communities they serve.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: This is not ideal given the cost to build AWH in an already affluent community is extremely high and severely impacts the number and quality of the units that can be built.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: On the contrary, AWH built nearby, in blighted or lower income areas, has many benefits. Those benefits include the ability to buy land at lower costs, build more and better-quality units, transform the blighted and lower income areas with investments in the community, including roads, sidewalks, funds for better municipal services, new and better infrastructure, community activities and programs and many other benefits that go along with large investments in new projects.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: In short, AWH investment is desired and necessary. It should be used as a double-edged sword to both provide needed housing and improve needy areas.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: This way, taxpayers and recipients get the biggest bang for their buck!

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: This one is easy: take all steps necessary to make certain our water and air are clean and that Florida holds polluters accountable.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Overcrowding in our State is taking hold in our large cities and traffic is approaching gridlock levels.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The problem is that our leaders believe it is possible to put 10 pounds of population into a 5-pound population bag!

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: It is not possible and is having the predictable effect.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Florida needs to continue to invest in improving and enlarging where possible, its roadways.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Florida also needs to look at common sense mass transportation alternatives like more rail, bus and other transportation modes which will help move our people from point to point.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The real elephant in the room, however, is the massive population growth our State has experienced. As I said earlier, there is a limit to the number of people one can cram into a fixed area, and in much of our State, we have hit that limit.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Stop building new housing until we can absorb the number of residents we currently have and start taking care of the Floridians who are already here and who deserve the quality of life they were promised and expect.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: In addition, rather than continue to build more new units, let’s fix the broken- and run-down units we already have, making housing better for all.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: If we stop making the problem worse by mindlessly adding more housing units, and fix and/or improve the housing units we already have, we might be able to preserve the amazing quality of life our current Florida residents envision, get our traffic nightmare under control and further increase the value of all our residents’ investment.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: All of that would be a home run for everyone.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Our country is woefully overindebted and its retirement promises are unkeepable, as our Social Security and Medicare unfunded amounts alone are equal to 10 years' worth of every penny the United States collects in revenue!

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: In other words, the system will fail, the only question is when?

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: We do not want this to happen to our retirees in Florida.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: While promises are nice, financial realities are something very different.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The State of Florida has one pension system, the Florida Retirement System, (FRS).

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The mechanism for paying the aforementioned pension obligations is an investment account managed by the State.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The required size of the investment account is determined by the revenue the account yields in relation to the number of retirees needing to be paid.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Currently the account itself has become unable, on its own, to pay the amounts the State is required to pay.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Given same, in order to “fix” the pension system, the State would currently have to inject $43B into the fund, an amount equal to almost 50% of the State’s entire budget.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Finally with respect to the above structure to pay retirees, in the case where the investment account begins to fail, is cut significantly or goes to zero, the State will likely bear the ENTIRE responsibility to come up with all of the funds, over $200B, a second time, to restore the investment account.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Given the size of the investment account, this alone could bankrupt the State and devastate our taxpayers.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The chances of this happening are not zero.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Contrast the above with a 401k type account for employees, with the State making very generous contributions; an account which each employee would own.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Unlike the defined benefit plan first described above, the 401K type account is a defined contribution benefit plan.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The 401k type plan has several benefits.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 1) It allows the employee to own their account, benefit from it and take it with them with no strings attached.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 2) Since the plan belongs to the employee they can invest and do with the funds in their account upon departure from the State as they wish.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 3) It allows the State to pay as you go, budget responsibly, not go into debt and retain employees by raising the State’s contribution to a level which would entice and financially motivate its employees.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Lastly a 401K type plan for all new employees, which is intelligently designed, would be good for those new employees, while honoring the promises made to existing employees, and at the same time protect Florida’s residents from making financial promises that they probably can’t afford to keep.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The truth is, in the Free State of Florida, the high property tax rate is choking residents and enabling unconscious elected leaders in our cities and school boards to spend like the flow of money is never-ending.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Given politicians are experts at talking, they will always have a reason why your paying more to them is necessary. Let's ignore that problem for a minute.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Property owners deserve relief and unconscious elected leaders need to do the hard work of caring for taxpayer money, by cutting their overall budgets by at least 5% and preferably 10%.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Floridians are continuously forced to tighten their belts, and the same should be required of government bureaucrats.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: For example, Florida school budgets have grown from $2.5 billion in 1980 to $29.7 billion in 2024, a 12-fold increase.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Meanwhile the 1980 median income for the average Floridian was about $18,000, and in 2024 that number grew to $72,000, only a 4-fold increase.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Worse the number of people living in Florida expected to pay for the 12-fold increase in school budgets has only about doubled since 1980.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The real question is, how do Floridians pay any bill that has gone up 12-times, with personal income that has only increased 4-times?

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: What’s the solution and how to implement it?

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Slash and eventually eliminate property taxes for residency vested Florida homeowners and renters.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: For each year beyond a year-ten residency vesting period requirement, Florida homeowners would be entitled to a cumulative 10%-point increase of their existing homestead exemption, until their adjusted exemption reaches 100%.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Renters in Florida, who meet the ten-year residency vesting period requirement and who go on to purchase a Florida home, would also enjoy the same cumulative 10%-point increase of their new home's homestead exemption, until their adjusted exemption reaches 100%.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Additionally and critically, the adjusted homestead exemption shall be transferable to the homeowner's wife or children.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 1) Immediately reduce the Florida Constitutional maximum property tax rate by 50%.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: This change would mean the potential maximum tax rate on one’s property would be necessarily dramatically reduced thereby reducing revenue to government by up to $18B.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 2) Reduce school spending by at least 5%, possibly 10%, directing those savings to property owners, reducing revenue to government by $1.5B to $3B.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 3) Reduce municipal spending by at least 5%, possibly 10%, saving property owners and reducing revenue to government by $1.5B to $3B.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 4) Reduce fraud and waste Statewide likely saving $3B to $5B.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 5) Other miscellaneous State and municipal savings of $1B.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 6) Note: Florida had a $21B surplus in its most recent budget. These funds should be added to Florida’s version of a savings account for emergencies only, the Budget Stabilization Fund (BSF).

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: 7) Last but not least, the law must be changed to allow homesteaded property owners the right to pass down properties to wives and children, without an increase in assessed value - which would otherwise make a family home instantly unaffordable and ensure that Florida families will all be involuntarily displaced.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: By taking all of the above-mentioned steps, the likely result would be that property values would increase, revenues to government would necessarily increase, property owners would receive desperately needed relief and government would be forced to spend the revenue it collects much more carefully.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Legal immigration is good. Uncontrolled, unvetted, unregulated, illegal immigration is bad.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: I support the responsible development of AI in Florida, provided it delivers clear benefits to Floridians and does not come at the expense of any of our residents.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: To that end, I would require the following conditions for any new data center:

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: As a condition of approval, each data center must commit to building or funding additional power generation and infrastructure sufficient to supply at least 120% of its actual power consumption. This obligation would remain in effect for the entire life of the project.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Additionally, data centers would be required to pay 110% of the electricity rate charged to residential customers, or 110% of the rate they normally pay, whichever is greater. The extra 10% would be credited back on a pro-rata basis to Florida’s residential ratepayers.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Supercharging Florida’s Forgotten – Tough Love Will Work Here, Just Like it Does at Home.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Florida’s poor don’t need another handout. They need a real shot — and the support to seize it.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: We have too many voiceless brothers and sisters trapped in slums, ghettos, and war-zone neighborhoods that no one should have to endure.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Enough is enough. We’re done subsidizing failure. We’re done watching good tax dollars vanish into programs that reward dependency and punish success.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: The failed “Live Local Act” and its clones are a disgrace: they deliver almost zero low-cost housing for struggling Floridians, bulldoze historic neighborhoods, and stuff millions into the pockets of connected developers and politicians. It’s corporate welfare dressed up as compassion.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Enter my proposed “Oasis Act” — a no-excuses, results-driven revolution.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Instead of scattering money to the wind, the Oasis Act redirects the exact same developer incentives to the worst, most dangerous, and forgotten slum parcels across Florida where the land is dirt-cheap.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: That means every state dollar stretches dramatically farther — and actually changes lives.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Ironclad security first. A hardened perimeter seals the entire site. One way in, one way out, with 24/7 security at the gate. Outside predators, gangs, drugs, and chaos are kept out. Period.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Safe, dignified housing rises next — clean, affordable units for families who want better. Parks, playgrounds, and real neighborhood features included.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Limited retail and offices go in — just enough to supply daily needs inside the Oasis. Residents will still do most of their shopping and work in the wider world.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Rigorous rules. Every resident signs on to accountability: no crime, no drugs, school attendance for kids, work or training requirements for adults. Break the rules, and your spot is given to another willing to follow the rules. This isn’t a free ride — it’s a launchpad for serious and committed people who are ready to climb.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Once the first Oasis proves it works, we replicate it aggressively until every blighted war zone area in Florida is transformed. One day the walls come down, the gates open, and what was a dangerous slum becomes another safe, thriving Florida neighborhood.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Bottom line: This is the biggest bang for the taxpayer housing buck Florida has ever seen.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: It gives our most disadvantaged citizens, who are willing to be accountable, a genuine, life-changing gateway out of poverty — not another trap disguised as “help.”

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: It gives our disadvantaged Floridians the tools, the safety, and the tough love they actually need to win.

passages.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passages.text: Florida deserves better. Our poorest deserve a real chance — and the rest of us deserve policies that finally work and rid our state of the blight that ruins the lives of too many.

passages.heading: Both Parties Want to Crush Us by Pretending We Don't Exist
passages.text: "First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you, then you win" Ghandi

passage.text: 4) Restore our insurance market back to pricing risk, reflected in policy premiums.

passage.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passage.text: In other words, this plan would bring back “ real ” insurance coverage and aggressive competition, which will see premiums reflect actual risk – not the unknown costs of subsidizing a market with no visible bottom.

passage.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passage.text: The likely best two solutions are: allow radical competition between ALL legitimate and financially strong insurance carriers. Encourage a wide menu of deductibles, so that if customers wish, they can participate in risk in return for lower premiums.

passage.heading: I'LL FIX IT...AND MAKE FLORIDA EVEN BETTER
passage.text: This plan keeps private insurers handling day-to-day administration and negotiation, uses loans instead of grants to reduce moral hazard, only applies full government control for the most extreme cases, and leaves the insurance market healthy, competing, and functioning with the most competitive premiums, exactly like it should function.

passage.heading: Below is the shortened version of my solutions for Florida
passage.text: Eliminate property taxes on homesteaded primary residences. Benefit passes down to children. Completely rewrite broken property and auto insurance laws. Dismiss non-criminal traffic tickets for drivers with clean 10-year records. Eliminate unfair paid highway express lanes. Eliminate unfair tolls on public roads. Eliminate Florida’s unfair gas tax. Eliminate permit fees to repair and improve your home. Force local government to provide water and sewer at cost. Slash bloated government, wherever it is, that we don’t need – or want. Rewrite the unaffordable, broken healthcare laws. Put doctors, not government and insurance companies, in charge. Make ‘Right to Try’ laws absolute.

passage.heading: Keep Florida affordable.
passage.text: Slash and eventually eliminate property taxes for vested Florida homeowners and renters. For each year beyond a year-ten residency vesting period requirement, Florida homeowners would be entitled to a cumulative 10%-point increase of their existing homestead exemption, until their adjusted exemption reaches 100%. Renters in Florida, who meet a ten-year residency vesting period requirement and who go on to purchase a Florida home, would also enjoy the same cumulative 10%-point increase of their new home's homestead exemption, until their adjusted exemption reaches 100%. Additionally, the adjusted homestead exemption shall be transferable to the homeowner's wife or children.
